'''Cameron Spencer''' (born April 6, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Loyola Greyhounds men's basketball|Loyola Greyhounds]], the [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers Scarlet Knights]], and the [[UConn Huskies men's basketball|UConn Huskies]].

==Early life==
Spencer grew up in [[Davidsonville, Maryland]], and attended the [[St. Paul's School for Boys]]. He was named the [[Maryland Interscholastic Athletic Association]] (MIAA) Player of the Year as a senior after he averaged 25 points, seven rebounds, and 4.5 assists per game.<ref name="animal" />

==College career==
Spencer began his college basketball career with the [[Loyola Greyhounds men's basketball|Loyola Greyhounds]]. He averaged ten points, 3.1 assists, and 3.4 rebounds in 23 games before suffering a hip injury and was named to the [[Patriot League]] All-Freshman team.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2021/03/09/boiling-to-return-from-hip-surgery-cameron-spencer-is-back-at-the-perfect-time-for-loyola-maryland-basketball/|title=Boiling' to return from hip surgery, Cameron Spencer is back at the perfect time for Loyola Maryland basketball|newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun]]|date=March 9, 2021|access-date=November 11, 2022}}</ref> Spencer missed most of his sophomore season while recovering from his hip injury. He returned for the final five games of the season and averaged 10.2 points.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.baltimoresun.com/2021/12/31/after-missing-much-of-last-season-to-recover-from-hip-surgery-cam-spencer-relishing-healthy-full-time-return-to-loyola-maryland-mens-basketball/|title=After missing much of last season to recover from hip surgery, Cam Spencer relishing healthy, full-time return to Loyola|newspaper=[[The Baltimore Sun]]|date=December 31, 2021|access-date=November 11, 2022}}</ref> Spencer was named first-team All-Patriot League as a junior after averaging 18.9 points, 4.8 rebounds, 3.2 assists, and 2.3 steals per game.<ref name="animal">{{cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/rutgersbasketball/2022/11/meet-rutgers-cam-spencer-a-competitive-animal-who-may-be-just-scratching-surface-of-his-potential.html|title=Meet Rutgers’ Cam Spencer: a competitive ‘animal’ eager to make B1G jump with Scarlet Knights|first=Brian|last=Fonseca|website=[[NJ.com]]|date=November 7, 2022|access-date=November 11, 2022}}</ref> Following the end of the season, Spencer entered the NCAA transfer portal.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/loyola/Article/College-basketball-transfer-portal-Cam-Spencer-Minnesota-Loyola-Chicago-185875157/|title=Loyola Maryland transfer Cam Spencer talks visits|first=Dushawn|last=London|website=[[247Sports]]|date=April 7, 2022|access-date=November 11, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/rutgersbasketball/2022/04/sharpshooting-transfer-cam-spencer-details-why-he-chose-rutgers-steve-pikiell.html|title=Sharpshooting transfer Cam Spencer details why he chose Rutgers, Steve Pikiell|first=Brian|last=Fonseca|website=[[NJ.com]]|date=April 19, 2022|access-date=November 11, 2022}}</ref>

Spencer ultimately transferred to [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball|Rutgers]] after also receiving interest from [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]] and [[NC State Wolfpack men's basketball|NC State]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/college/rutgers/2022/04/19/rutgers-basketball-adds-transfer-cam-spencer-guard-loyola/7369445001/|title=Rutgers basketball adds transfer Cam Spencer, guard from Loyola|work=[[Asbury Park Press]]|date=April 19, 2022|access-date=November 11, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.onthebanks.com/2022/4/19/23030201/first-team-all-patriot-league-guard-cam-spencer-commits-rutgers-basketball-big-ten-loyola-maryland|title=First Team All-Patriot League guard Cam Spencer commits to Rutgers|first=Aaron|last=Breitman|website=OnTheBanks.com|publisher=[[SB Nation]]|date=April 19, 2022|access-date=November 16, 2022}}</ref> He entered the 2022–23 as a starting guard for the Scarlet Knights.<ref>{{cite  news|url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/college/rutgers/2022/11/08/rutgers-basketball-cam-spencer-wows-crowd-in-debut/69625384007/|title=Rutgers basketball: Cam Spencer wows crowd in debut|newspaper=[[Asbury Park Press]]|date=November 8, 2022|access-date=November 14, 2022}}</ref> Spencer scored 14 points on 6-of-8 shooting, including a go-ahead three-point shot with 13.3 seconds left, in Rutgers' 65–64 upset win over top-ranked [[2022–23 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/rutgers-stuns-top-ranked-purdue-again-behind-winning-3-pointer-from-cam-spencer-043016688.html|title=Rutgers stuns top-ranked Purdue, again, behind winning 3-pointer from Cam Spencer|first=Ryan|last=Young|website=[[Yahoo! Sports]]|date=January 2, 2023|access-date=January 5, 2023}}</ref> Spencer was named the [[Big Ten Conference]] Player of the Week after scored another go-ahead three pointer with 15 seconds left and scored 23 points overall in a 65–62 win against [[2022–23 Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball team|Northwestern]] on January 11, 2023,  and scored 21 points with six rebounds, six assists, and four steals as Rutgers beat [[2022–23 Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball team|Ohio State]] 68–64.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/rutgers/Article/Cam-Spencer-earns-Big-Ten-co-player-of-the-week-203152482/|title=Cam Spencer earns Big Ten co-player of the week|first=Bobby|last=Deren|website=[[247Sports]]|date=January 17, 2023|access-date=January 19, 2023}}</ref> He finished the season averaging 13.2 points, 3.8 rebounds, 3.1 assists, and two steals per game.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/college/rutgers/Article/Cam-Spencer-delivers-for-Rutgers-despite-being-underutilized-206786449/|title=Cam Spencer delivers for Rutgers despite being underutilized|first=Bobby|last=Deen|website=[[247Sports]]|date=March 18, 2023|access-date=March 20, 2023}}</ref> After the season, Spencer decided to utilize the extra year of eligibility granted to college athletes who played in the 2020 season due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic]] and entered the NCAA transfer portal for a second time.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/college/rutgers/2023/05/19/rutgers-basketball-guard-cam-spencer-enters-transfer-portal/70232598007/|title=Rutgers basketball: Cam Spencer enters transfer portal, a late hit to 2023-24 roster|newspaper=[[Asbury Park Press]]|date=May 19, 2023|access-date=May 26, 2023}}</ref>

Spencer transferred to UConn.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/37809324/uconn-lands-sharp-shooting-transfer-guard-cam-spencer|title=Sources: UConn lands sharpshooting transfer guard Cam Spencer|first=Jeff|last=Borzello|website=[[ESPN.com]]|date=June 7, 2023|access-date=June 7, 2023}}</ref> He was named first-team All-[[Big East Conference]] after starting all 40 of the Huskies' games and averaging 14.3 points, 4.9 rebounds, 3.6 assists, and 1.5 steals per game as UConn won the national championship<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nj.com/rutgersbasketball/2024/04/how-cam-spencer-paul-mulcahy-rutgers-basketball-transfers-performed-in-2023-24-season.html|title=Cam Spencer won a title with UConn, but what about Paul Mulcahy, other Rutgers transfers?|first=Brian|last=Fonseca|website=[[NJ.com]]|date=April 9, 2024|access-date=May 31, 2024}}</ref> Spencer scored 11 points with eight rebounds, two assists, and two steals in UConn's 75–60 win over [[2023–24 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]] in the [[2024 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|National Championship game]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ctinsider.com/sports/uconn-mens-basketball/article/cam-spencer-final-four-ncaa-championship-huskies-19393679.php|title=UConn guard Cam Spencer fulfills dream with NCAA title in one season.|website=CT Insider|date=April 9, 2024|access-date=May 31, 2024}}</ref>

==Professional career==
On June 27, 2024, Spencer was selected in the second round with the 53rd overall pick by the [[Detroit Pistons]] in the [[2024 NBA draft]]. However, on draft night he was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Joe|last=Arruda|title=Former UConn guard Cam Spencer with 53rd pick, heading to Memphis Grizzlies|url=https://www.courant.com/2024/06/27/former-uconn-guard-cam-spencer-with-53rd-pick-heading-to-memphis-grizzlies/|work=Hartford Courant|date=June 27, 2024|access-date=June 28, 2024}}</ref> On July 8, he signed a [[two-way contract]] with the Grizzlies.<ref>{{cite tweet|author=Grizzlies PR|title=The @memgrizz today signed Cam Spencer to a two-way contract.|number=1810467045005258842|user=GrizzliesPR|date=July 8, 2024|access-date=July 14, 2024}}</ref> On December 2, while playing for the [[Memphis Hustle]] of the [[NBA G League]], Spencer scored 51 points, including 12 three–pointers made.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Watch: Memphis Grizzlies rookie Cam Spencer explodes for 51 points in G League game|url=https://www.commercialappeal.com/story/sports/nba/grizzlies/2024/12/02/cam-spencer-highlights-g-league-memphis-grizzlies-hustle/76719681007/|access-date=December 11, 2024|website=commercialappeal.com|language=nl}}</ref> On January 10, 2025, Spencer suffered a fractured left thumb that necessitated surgery, and was ruled out for at least three weeks.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Grizzlies' Cam Spencer: May not return to playing|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-cam-spencer-out-with-fractured-thumb/amp/|access-date=January 12, 2025|website=cbssports.com|language=en}}</ref> He made 25 appearances (one start) for Memphis during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 4.2 points, 1.2 rebounds, and 1.4 assists.

On June 30, 2025, Spencer re-signed with the Grizzlies on a two-year, $4.5 million contract; the deal was later restructured to a four-year, $10.5 million contract on July 16.<ref>{{cite web | title=Grizzlies' Cam Spencer: Deal being restructured | website=CBS Sports | date=2025-07-14 | url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-cam-spencer-deal-being-restructured/ | access-date=2025-12-06}}</ref>

On December 15, 2025, Spencer had his best offensive outing with 27 points and 6 assists on 7/10 shooting from behind the arc, rallying the Grizzlies to an 121-103 blowout win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-12-16 |title=Grizzlies' Cam Spencer: Hits for 27 points in victory |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/grizzlies-cam-spencer-hits-for-27-points-in-victory/ |access-date=2025-12-16 |website=CBS Sports |language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Spencer's older brother, [[Pat Spencer (basketball)|Pat]], was a four-time All-American and won the [[Tewaaraton Award]] as a lacrosse player at Loyola before playing a season of college basketball at Northwestern.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.wmar2news.com/sports/local-sports/another-spencer-sparking-loyola|title=Another Spencer sparking Loyola|first=Shawn|last=Stepner|website=[[WMAR-TV]]|date=January 27, 2022|access-date=November 16, 2022}}</ref> Pat now plays basketball professionally for the [[Phoenix Suns]] of the [[National Basketball Association]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://arizonasports.com/nba/phoenix-suns/suns-2-way-contract-g-pat-spencer-official|title=Suns officially agree to 2-way contract with former Warriors guard Pat Spencer|first=Payne|last=Moses|work=[[Arizona Sports]]|date=July 4, 2026|access-date=August 3, 2026}}</ref>
